Synopsis:
    A federal judge dismissed a lawsuit by British anti-disinformation activist Imran Ahmed (CEO of the Center for Countering Digital Hate) that sought to block the Trump administration from detaining and deporting him. While the judge acknowledged Ahmed may have valid claims, jurisdiction was ruled out under a recent appellate decision. A short grace period preserves the restraining order to allow appeal. The case sits within a broader pattern of Trump administration visa/green card revocations targeting foreign nationals over political speech and disinformation-related activities, which continues to generate fragmented and conflicting court rulings.
